content: Erythromycin lactobionate can increase the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered serious, and alternative medications should be used. Both erythromycin lactobionate and levoketoconazole can prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or substitution with other drugs. Erythromycin lactobionate can decrease the levels or effects of oral contraceptives containing levonorgestrel, ethinyl estradiol, and ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised, as antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Erythromycin lactobionate and lithium both increase the QTc interval, posing a serious risk. Alternative medications should be used to avoid this interaction. Erythromycin lactobionate and lofepramine both prolong the QTc interval, making their concurrent use a serious concern. Alternative drugs should be considered. Erythromycin lactobionate significantly increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, as lomitapide levels can rise several-fold, leading to severe toxicity. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated because lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is not recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases loperamide levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are required. Erythromycin lactobionate increases lopinavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and lopinavir increases erythromycin lactobionate levels through the same mechanism. This bidirectional interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Erythromycin lactobionate increases loratadine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. Lorlatinib decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate increases lovastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated because strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can significantly increase systemic statin exposure, raising the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Erythromycin lactobionate increases lumateperone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The lumateperone dose should be reduced to 21 mg/day when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Erythromycin lactobionate and lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Lumefantrine decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while erythromycin lactobionate increases lumefantrine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Erythromycin lactobionate increases lurasidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. The manufacturer advises reducing the starting dose of lurasidone to 20 mg/day and the maximum daily dose to 80 mg when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Concurrent use may increase the risk of lurasidone-related adverse reactions. Erythromycin lactobionate increases levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Erythromycin lactobionate and macimorelin both prolong the QTc interval. Macimorelin increases the QTc interval by approximately 11 milliseconds. Coadministration with drugs that prolong the QT interval should be avoided to reduce the risk of torsade de pointes-type ventricular tachycardia. Sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs is recommended before administering macimorelin. Erythromycin lactobionate and maprotiline both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Erythromycin lactobionate increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Marijuana increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Erythromycin lactobionate increases mavacamten levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may necessitate a reduced mavacamten dose. Mavorixafor increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, while erythromycin lactobionate increases mavorixafor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation, and QTc monitoring is recommended in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Erythromycin lactobionate increases mefloquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate increases mestranol levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and decreases mestranol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Close monitoring is recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate and methadone both prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin lactobionate increases methadone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Erythromycin lactobionate increases methylprednisolone levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Methylprednisolone decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. Metronidazole increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Miconazole vaginal increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibacterial agents may reduce the efficacy of microbiota oral products containing bacterial spores. Antibiotic regimens should be completed 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. Erythromycin lactobionate increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Coadministration of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam increases systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. Erythromycin lactobionate increases mifepristone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Mifepristone increases erythromycin lactobionate levels through the same mechanism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate and mipomersen both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Liver function tests (LFTs) should be monitored closely. Erythromycin lactobionate and mirtazapine both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Mitotane decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4, and dosage adjustments may be necessary when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. Close monitoring is recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases mitoxantrone levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate increases mizolastine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Erythromycin lactobionate increases momelotinib toxicity by inhibiting OATP1B1/B3 transporters. Plasma concentrations of momelotinib may increase, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Close monitoring is recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases montelukast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Nafcillin decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases nafcillin effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases naldemedine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate increases naloxegol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Nefazodone increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Erythromycin lactobionate increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Nelfinavir increases erythromycin lactobionate levels through the same mechanism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Erythromycin lactobionate increases neomycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate increases neratinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Coadministration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. Nevirapine decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases niacin levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate increases nicardipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Erythromycin lactobionate increases nifedipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Initiating nifedipine at the lowest available dose is recommended when coadministered with erythromycin lactobionate. Erythromycin lactobionate increases nilotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Nilotinib increases erythromycin lactobionate levels through the same mechanism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used.
